paragraphs: I'm applying for the FP&A Sr. Analyst role at Two Sigma. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. What drew me to this role is the focus on compute spend. At a firm built on engineering and research, how you plan for that spend and charge it out is a real business question, and you want the answers in dashboards people can use.

At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%, ran variance and sensitivity analyses on budget changes, and created AI powered dashboards that combined predictive metrics with financial projections. At JPMorgan Asset Management I worked on budget allocation across marketing channels. I built models to evaluate how to deploy $10M and benchmarked past allocations, which identified 30% in efficiency gains.

That maps to the annual planning, monthly reporting and scenario tooling you describe for the Engineering area. My background is corporate finance and analytics rather than cloud cost management, so that part would be new to me. I'd bring the habits that matter here: making sure the numbers tie, and explaining them plainly to the people who rely on them. I'd welcome the chance to talk about the role.
